## Summary
Implements **Issue #34** — reopen the commissioning window on a device that's already part of our fabric so a second ecosystem (Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa, …) can commission it without a factory reset.

- New subcommands: `matter @N commission open-window` (ECM, plus `--basic` for BCM) and `matter @N commission close-window`.
- `ComputePAKEVerifier(passcode, salt, iterations)` derives the 97-byte `(w0 || L)` verifier using the existing SPAKE2+ primitives; random passcode / salt / discriminator generators included with spec-constrained bounds.
- TLV payload is encoded via `tlv.NewWriter` directly (the generated `AdministratorCommissioning` struct uses a `tlv:",bytes"` tag that's not wired into the marshaler).
- Runs as a Timed Invoke. Uses the session daemon when available, falls back to a direct CASE session otherwise.
- Daemon's `InvokeResp` now carries `ClusterStatus` so cluster-specific status codes (`Busy`, `PAKEParameterError`, `WindowNotOpen`) and generic IM status codes (e.g. `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND`) surface consistently whether the daemon handles the call or not.
- Window subcommands override `commission`'s daemon-guard `PersistentPreRunE` because they only invoke a command; they don't need the BoltDB lock.
- Setup payload for the QR / manual code gets VID/PID from the local store, falling back to reading `BasicInformation` over CASE; read failures are non-fatal (VID/PID default to 0).

## Test plan
- [x] `mise run test` — all packages green (new `verifier_test.go` covers composition, determinism, input bounds, generator diversity).
- [x] `mise exec -- go build ./...` clean.
- [x] End-to-end against a matter.js virtual On/Off light:
  - [x] `open-window` prints QR / manual / passcode / discriminator / salt / expiry; device log confirms all 5 TLV fields decoded correctly.
  - [x] `AdministratorCommissioning.WindowStatus` reads `1` (EnhancedWindowOpen) after open, `0` (WindowNotOpen) after close.
  - [x] `close-window` on a closed device → `WindowNotOpen` cluster-status decoded to friendly error.
  - [x] Second `open-window` while one is active → `Busy` cluster-status decoded to friendly error.
  - [x] `--basic` against matter.js returns IM `UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND (0x81)` (expected — matter.js doesn't advertise the BC feature).
- [ ] Live hardware smoke test (not run — reviewer's call).

Closes #34

author: ebongard
body:
## Problem

The agent entered infinite retry loops on ``lade Rechnung hoch``-style requests: it invoked ``mcp.paperless.upload_document`` with a literal placeholder string (``\"base64_encoded_content_of_the_invoice\"``) because the LLM never sees the bytes of an attached file — only the OCR text. Paperless rejected the garbage with opaque HTTP 400s. Related MIME and DNS-level fixes in #429, ``renfield-mcp-paperless#3``/``#4`` addressed the 403 and the silent-decode path, but the root cause — an agent tool that requires data the agent doesn't have — remained.

## Fix

A new platform internal tool **``internal.forward_attachment_to_paperless(attachment_id, …)``**. It reads the real ``ChatUpload`` row + file from storage, base64-encodes the bytes, and invokes ``mcp.paperless.upload_document`` under the hood. The agent never handles raw bytes — it only passes an integer ID.

### Plumbing

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| ``services/chat_upload_tool.py`` *(new)* | ``CHAT_UPLOAD_TOOLS`` dict + async handler, analogous to ``knowledge_tool.py`` |
| ``services/agent_tools.py`` | ``_register_internal_tools`` merges new tools alongside ``KNOWLEDGE_TOOL`` |
| ``services/action_executor.py`` | Explicit dispatch for the new intent (it needs ``self.mcp_manager``) |
| ``api/websocket/chat_handler.py`` | ``_fetch_document_context`` passes ``attachment_id`` into the templates |
| ``prompts/chat.yaml`` *(de + en)* | Templates expose ``[attachment_id=N]`` marker and forwarding hint |
| ``prompts/agent.yaml`` — ``agent_prompt_documents`` *(de + en)* | Rule: use ``internal.forward_attachment_to_paperless``, never raw ``mcp.paperless.upload_document`` with invented base64 |
| ``config/agent_roles.yaml`` | Documents role adds the new internal tool |
| ``config/mcp_servers.yaml`` | ``upload_document`` removed from ``paperless.prompt_tools`` (still discoverable by direct-code callers via ``all_discovered_tools``) |

### Direct-code path unchanged

The frontend's ``/api/chat_upload/{id}/paperless`` endpoint (``chat_upload.forward_to_paperless``) keeps working — it calls ``manager.execute_tool(\"mcp.paperless.upload_document\", …)`` by name, which lookups against ``all_discovered_tools``, not the ``prompt_tools``-filtered set.

## Test

``tests/backend/test_chat_upload_tool.py`` covers nine cases:

1. Missing ``attachment_id``
2. Non-integer ``attachment_id``
3. Missing ``mcp_manager``
4. Attachment not in DB
5. File missing from disk
6. Happy path — asserts MCP receives **real** base64 matching on-disk bytes
7. ``title`` overrides filename
8. MCP failure surfaces detail to the agent
9. Malformed MCP response yields ``success=True`` with ``task_id=None``

Template rendering was dry-run in the prod pod with both ``de`` and ``en``; all three templates (``document_context_section``, ``document_separator``, ``document_context_multi_section``) produce the ``[attachment_id=N]`` marker cleanly.

## Relation to other PRs

- ``renfield-mcp-paperless#3`` (merged, deployed) — fixed MIME type ``application/octet-stream`` → ``application/pdf``
- ``renfield-mcp-paperless#4`` (open) — strict base64 validation, defensive against future misuse
- **This PR** — architectural fix: agent no longer has the hallucination surface

## Test plan

- [x] ``py_compile`` on all 5 edited Python files + new test file
- [x] YAML parse + key integrity on all 4 edited YAML files
- [x] Template rendering dry-run (4 lang × template combinations)
- [ ] CI unit tests (9 new in ``test_chat_upload_tool.py``)
- [ ] Manual E2E: attach PDF in chat, say ``lade nach Paperless`` — agent must call ``internal.forward_attachment_to_paperless`` with the shown attachment_id, real bytes reach Paperless, task_id returned

## Summary

This is the first substantive PR against `main`; it brings the repository from the initial scaffolding (README + empty solution) up to a working single-user Telegram bot that executes Codex-backed turns with durable approval gating. It covers every implemented backlog task so far — the remote `main` is behind, so a single PR is the only path to publish them.

Task-by-task (in commit order, oldest first):

- **T-005** — .NET Worker Service host and Windows Service lifecycle
- **T-006** — Durable Serilog logging for service-critical events
- **T-007** — File-backed `IStateStore` with atomic JSON writes and quarantine-on-corruption
- **T-008** — Telegram long-polling intake with owner-only filtering
- **T-009** — `/agent` and `/project` commands; per-chat active agent and per-agent project binding
- **T-010** — Project catalog discovery + refusal on no-active-project
- **T-011** — Thread mapping persistence and `/clear` rotation (history-preserving)
- **T-025** — `Stryker.NET` scaffolding and the advisory mutation-check step in `/implement-next-task`
- **T-012** — Per-context turn queue (`PerContextTurnQueue`) and `ITurnExecutor` seam
- **T-013** — `BackendProcessSupervisor` with bounded restart backoff
- **T-014** — `stdio` JSON-RPC transport adapter for `codex app-server`
- **T-015** — End-to-end Telegram → Codex → Telegram turn execution
- **T-016** — Durable approval handling + `/approve` / `/deny` commands (this session)

## T-016 highlights (this session's work)

- `IApprovalCoordinator` blocks the executing turn on a per-approval `TaskCompletionSource<ApprovalDecision>` until the owner resolves it; the backend's global `activeTurn` stays live and the per-context queue's ordering guarantees are preserved.
- Pending `ApprovalRecord` is persisted under `state/approvals/pending/` **before** the Telegram notification is sent; on resolve it moves to `state/approvals/resolved/` with the decision, timestamps, and operation metadata for audit.
- `/approve <id>` and `/deny <id>` enforce chat-scope isolation per US-09 — a command from the wrong chat is rejected without touching state.
- Immediate ACK on `/approve` / `/deny`; the final backend answer arrives later through the executor's existing `IChatReplySink` path.
- Stale-record sweep and restart-aware recovery are explicitly deferred to T-018.

- `ApprovalRecord` and `ApprovalContext` retain `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`; T-023 owns removing those markers when the mutation gate expands.

author: hawkw
body:
In order to be able to make changes to the sled-agent API's VMM state types, they must be able to participate in API versioning. Presently, these types cannot, as they appear in both the server-side-versioned sled-agent API (which is fine), and the client-side-versioned Nexus internal API (which is not fine, as the Nexus API is client-side versioned, and client-side versioning is not a real thing yet). In #10290, I described this problem in greater detail, and proposed a solution: we change the flow of VMM state data between Nexus and sled-agent so that the VMM state information is *only* transferred via a sled-agent API of which Nexus is a client, rather than being sent in both sled-agent responses to Nexus requests *and* in sled-agent requests to Nexus. 

In the current code, sled-agent calls Nexus' `cpapi_instances_put` endpoint to send Nexus a new VMM state in the request body. In #10303, I described changing this so that it is instead simply treated as a "doorbell" notification from the sled-agent that the instance's state has changed, and that Nexus will then handle the doorbell by requesting the current state from the sled-agent. This PR makes that change. Now, Nexus will ignore the `SledVmmState` body sent in `cpapi_instances_put` and then request the current state from the sled-agent. This makes it fine to have the client-side-versioned Nexus API always take the `v1` version of `SledVmmState`, because it doesn't actually look at it. Subsequently, we will introduce a new API which does not take a body at all, and both the new API and the current one will call into the same code path in Nexus.

In order to do this, it was necessary to change sled-agent so that requests to get a VMM's state no longer go into the single request channel to the VMM's `InstanceRunner` task. I described why this is necessary in [this comment][1], but basically, in the current sled-agent implementation, requests to get the VMM's state are not processed until the state change event from the `InstanceMonitor` task (which watches the Propolis instance state) has finished being processed. Processing the state change involves sending the new state to Nexus, which is retried until a Nexus replica confirms that it has written the new state to CRDB. In the current code, where Nexus' GET request for the current state is not handled until the state change has been completed, the request from Nexus in response to the doorbell ringing will always time out. It is necessary for this to remain synchronous and prevent the sled-agent's state machine from advancing to the next state change until Nexus has acknowledged the current one, or else Nexus may miss state changes. Therefore, I have changed the sled-agent so that the VMM's current state is shared between the `InstanceRunner` task and the `Instance` handle via an `Arc<RwLock<InstanceStates>>`, so that the GET request can read it even while the `InstanceRunner` is doing something else. For more detail on this, see [this comment][2] on #10290, and [this comment on this PR explaining why it's an `RwLock`][3].

[1]: https://github.com/oxidecomputer/omicron/issues/10290#issuecomment-4306116311
[2]: https://github.com/oxidecomputer/omicron/issues/10290#issuecomment-4306116311
[3]: https://github.com/oxidecomputer/omicron/pull/10303#discussion_r3139291747

## Summary

- Adds a new `storage:oci` module implementing `StorageBackend` using the native OCI Java SDK (v3.67.3)
- Supports three authentication modes via `oci.auth.type`: `config_file` (default), `instance_principal`, and `workload_identity` (OKE)
- Implements multipart upload with configurable part size (5MiB–2GiB), single-file upload for small objects, fetch with range support, and sequential delete (OCI has no batch delete API)
- Includes full test coverage: `OciStorageConfigTest`, `OciStorageTest`, `OciUploadOutputStreamTest`

## Key design decisions

- Self-contained module — no refactoring of existing S3/GCS modules
- Uses native OCI SDK instead of S3-compatible API to support workload identity (OKE requires `OkeWorkloadIdentityAuthenticationDetailsProvider`, not static Customer Secret Keys)
- Delete is idempotent — 404 responses are silently ignored, matching S3 behavior
- Abort failures during error handling use `addSuppressed` to preserve the original exception
- `StorageTier` lookup uses stream-based matching on `toString()` rather than `valueOf()` for safety

## Summary

Fixes two CRITICAL CodeQL `py/partial-ssrf` findings in the OneDrive cloud storage adapter. Admin-authored `CloudStorageTarget.credentials` were flowing `tenant_id` / `drive_id` unvalidated into Microsoft Graph URLs — the OAuth token endpoint (`login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/...`) and the drives endpoint (`graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/drives/{drive_id}/...`). A malformed identifier could redirect Graph calls to an attacker-controlled origin, exposing `client_secret` during OAuth exchange.

- Bead: `enhancedchannelmanager-zbt74` (P0)
- CodeQL alerts: **1361**, **1362**
- Earlier Security triage specified the belt-and-suspenders pattern applied here

## Fix

Shape validators applied at **two** layers (per Security triage):

1. **API ingress** — `field_validator` on `CloudTargetCreateRequest`, `CloudTargetUpdateRequest`, and `CloudTargetTestRequest` rejects bad identifiers with HTTP 422 before touching the DB or adapter
2. **Adapter `__init__`** — `OneDriveAdapter` raises `ValueError` as defense-in-depth, ensuring direct adapter callers also get validation

Validators:
- `_TENANT_ID_RE` — anchored GUID or DNS domain (Azure AD valid shapes)
- `_DRIVE_ID_RE` — base64url-style (alnum + `!`, `_`, `-`), length-capped

## Files touched

- `backend/cloud_storage/onedrive_adapter.py` (+62 / -3)
- `backend/routers/export.py` (+27 / -1)
- `backend/tests/test_cloud_storage.py` (+186 / 0)

## Tests

New test classes in `backend/tests/test_cloud_storage.py`:
- `TestOneDriveTenantIdValidator` — GUID, domain, single-label pass; 18 hostile inputs rejected (`../evil`, `https://evil.com/`, `..%2Fattacker`, null-byte, overlong, double-dot, etc.)
- `TestOneDriveDriveIdValidator` — base64url pass; 13 hostile inputs rejected (path sep, percent-encoding, unicode, overlong, etc.)
- `TestOneDriveCloudTargetApiValidation` — via `async_client` (TestClient), confirms HTTP 422 on POST `/api/export/cloud-targets` and POST `/api/export/cloud-targets/test` with malicious `tenant_id` / `drive_id`, and HTTP 201 on the known-good payload

**Full backend suite:** `2305 passed in 45.04s`

## Container verification

Deployed via `docker cp` + `docker restart ecm-ecm-1`, then issued a bearer token and confirmed:
- Valid OneDrive POST (`tenant_id=contoso.onmicrosoft.com`, `drive_id=b!abcDEF-_123`) -> HTTP 201
- Malicious `tenant_id="../evil"` -> HTTP 422 with clear `tenant_id must be an Azure AD GUID or verified domain name` message
- Malicious `drive_id="../../etc/passwd"` -> HTTP 422 with clear `drive_id must be a base64url-style Microsoft Graph identifier` message

## Dismissal policy

The earlier Security persona triage approved this as the canonical fix. Once this lands, CodeQL alerts 1361 and 1362 should auto-close on the next scan. No dismissal-as-false-positive needed.

- [x] New API-layer 422 tests pass
- [x] Existing OneDrive happy-path test (`TestOneDriveAdapter.test_test_connection_success`) still passes
- [x] Full backend suite green (2305 passed)

## Summary

- Notch list was showing raw XML like `<command-message>init</command-message> <c…` whenever a slash command (e.g. `/init`) was the first user message in a session.
- Root cause: `ConversationParser` filtered command wrappers with three `hasPrefix` checks (`<command-name>`, `<local-command`, `Caveat:`). Claude Code actually emits several sibling tags — `<command-message>`, `<command-args>`, `<local-command-stdout>`, `<local-command-caveat>`, `<local-command-stderr>` — and for `/init` the content starts with `<command-message>`, bypassing the filter entirely.
- Fix: replace the ad-hoc prefix checks with `isCommandOnlyContent(_:)`, which strips every `<command-*>` and `<local-command-*>` wrapper via regex (non-greedy, `[\s\S]*?`) and only filters when nothing meaningful remains. All four call sites in `ConversationParser` now route through this helper.

## Why strip-then-check instead of `isMeta`

Inspected a real session's JSONL: among user messages wrapped in `<command-*>` tags, `isMeta=true` was present in only 7/17 cases (the rest had the field absent). `isMeta` therefore cannot be relied on. Strip-then-check is also forward-compatible with any future `<command-xxx>` tag Claude Code adds, and correctly preserves real user text interleaved with wrappers (e.g. `<command-name>/foo</command-name>\n用户的真实补充`).

## Test plan

- [x] Release build succeeds (`xcodebuild -scheme ClaudeIsland -configuration Debug build`)
- [x] Standalone regex verification against fixture cases using real `NSRegularExpression`:
  - `<command-message>init</command-message>\n<command-name>/init</command-name>\n<command-args></command-args>` → filtered ✅ (was broken)
  - `<command-name>/foo</command-name>\n用户的真实补充` → kept (shows "用户的真实补充") ✅
  - `<local-command-stdout>hello</local-command-stdout>` → filtered ✅
  - `<local-command-caveat>...</local-command-caveat>` → filtered ✅
  - `Caveat: …` → filtered ✅
  - Regular Chinese/English user messages → kept ✅
- [x] Re-parsed a real session (119 user messages, containing the reported `<command-message>init</command-message>` case): 9 filtered, 110 kept, no real messages lost.

Adds a config file schema (`mode`, `rules`, `settings`) so teams can tune Gatekeeper per-repo without touching workflow YAML.

## Changes

### `action.yml`
- New optional `config` input — defaults to `.github/gatekeeper.yml`

### `index.js`
- `loadConfig()` — parses YAML config; safe defaults when file is absent or malformed
- `buildCliArgs()` — appends `--config <path>` to the vireon CLI call when the file exists
- `buildComment()` — respects `settings.comments.summary` and `settings.comments.explain_why`; adds *(advisory)* badge in the heading
- **Advisory mode**: `core.warning` instead of `core.setFailed` when `mode: advisory` and verdict is `fail`

### `README.md`
- Documented all config keys, accepted values, and defaults

## Example config

```yaml
# .github/gatekeeper.yml
mode: advisory          # "strict" (default) blocks the PR; "advisory" warns only

rules:
  - semantic-drift
  - architecture-boundaries
  - naming-conventions

settings:
  drift:
    sensitivity: medium   # low | medium | high
  comments:
    summary: true
    explain_why: true     # per-issue "why" text instead of raw JSON
```

The `authlib==1.7.0` release introduced an implicitly required dependency on `joserfc`. This causes an error when `jupyter_server_mcp` is imported:

body:
## Summary

- Fixes the "Failed to create camp entry" error when a user adds a camp the app hasn't seen before.
- Adds an RLS policy migration so authenticated users can create the stub "User-submitted" organization that new camps hang off of.
- Adds high-fidelity HTML mockups of the proposed redesigned Add Camp flow (name-first modal + URL-first right-side drawer).

## Root cause of the bug

`submitCamp` in `src/lib/actions.ts` needs a "User-submitted" organization to attach user-added stubs to. Three compounding issues broke that on a fresh DB:

1. The insert tried to write a non-existent `is_active` column on `organizations`.
2. The `organizations` table had RLS enabled with a SELECT-only policy — migrations 012 and 014 added insert policies for `sessions`, `activity_locations`, and `activities` but missed `organizations`.
3. The insert only destructured `data`, swallowing the error. `orgId` came back `null`, the downstream `activities` insert violated `organization_id NOT NULL`, and the user saw the generic "Failed to create camp entry."

## Changes

- **`supabase/migrations/018_organizations_user_insert.sql`** (new) — RLS insert policy on `organizations` for authenticated users. Mirrors the pattern from migrations 012/014.
- **`src/lib/actions.ts`** — stub-org creation now upserts on the existing `unique(name)` constraint, captures the error, and returns a clear message on failure. Also surfaced the previously swallowed `planner_entries` insert error for week-scoped adds.
- **`public/mockups/add-camp.html`** (new) — static design mockup page (routing overview + every state of the proposed name flow and URL drawer). Visible at `/mockups/add-camp.html` once deployed, or [click here](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rachelarteaga/kidtinerary/claude/fix-camp-creation-ZpTkR/public/mockups/add-camp.html) to preview from the branch.

## ⚠ Post-merge step required

Migration 018 needs to be applied to your Supabase project — it is **not** automatic on Vercel deploy. After merging, paste this into the Supabase SQL editor:

```sql
create policy "Authenticated users can insert organizations"
  on organizations for insert
  to authenticated
  with check (true);
```

Or run `supabase db push` if you use the Supabase CLI locally.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — all 164 existing tests pass
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean on `actions.ts`
- [ ] After merge + migration 018 applied: add a camp with a brand-new name (e.g. "Test Camp XYZ") from the planner — should succeed, no "Failed to create camp entry"
- [ ] Add a camp scoped to a specific week + kid — planner entry should appear on that cell
- [ ] Existing (directory-matched) camps still add correctly

body:
## Summary

- `@perfetto` now runs `Profile.Allocs` in parallel with the CPU profiler and renders the samples as a dedicated "Allocations" track in the same Perfetto trace — no new API surface.
- Each alloc span's width = allocation size, scaled to fit the CPU wall-time range, so Perfetto's flame-graph tab reads as **total bytes per function**.
- Samples are sorted by stack so similar allocations cluster into fat bars, and the allocated type is appended as a synthetic leaf frame for slicing by type.

## Notes for reviewers

- `Profile.Allocs` samples carry no timestamp and no thread info, so the allocation track's time axis is synthetic — it's ordered for visual clarity, not causality. Only the flame-graph aggregation is semantically meaningful (total bytes per function).
- Default `sample_rate = 0.01` to keep overhead bounded on alloc-heavy workloads.
- We drive `Profile.Allocs` via `start`/`stop` rather than its `@profile` macro because Julia's hygiene pass renames the `sample_rate` kwarg when the macro is nested inside our own `quote`, causing `UndefKeywordError: sample_rate`. There's a comment in [src/macro.jl](src/macro.jl) explaining this.
- `perfetto_view` / `perfetto_open` gain an optional `alloc_results` kwarg for manual use.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing test suite passes
- [x] Smoke test: `@perfetto` on an alloc-heavy loop produces a trace with both pid=1 (CPU) and pid=2 (Allocations) events, with frames like `materialize`, `copy`, `similar` as expected

author: adamgell
body:
## Summary

Adds `.github/workflows/publish-api.yml` — a GHCR publish pipeline for
the `api-server` image — plus a `docs/release.md` runbook. Removes the
"rebuild from source on BigMac every deploy" friction so a follow-up on
the Ansible `compose_stack` role can pull `ghcr.io/adamgell/cmtraceopen-api`
instead of building.

## Trigger

- **Tag push**: `api-v*` (e.g. `api-v0.1.0`, `api-v0.2.0-rc.1`) — the
  `api-v` prefix keeps api-server releases separate from any future
  viewer / wasm-parser tags.
- **`workflow_dispatch`**: manual re-publish, with a `push` input
  (`true`/`false`) for dry-run builds.

## What it produces

Image: `ghcr.io/adamgell/cmtraceopen-api`

Platforms: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64` (ARM64 built under QEMU
emulation — expect a ~15–25 min build on the arm64 leg).

Tag shape, derived from the git tag via `docker/metadata-action`:
- `api-v0.1.0` → `0.1.0`, `0.1`, `latest`
- `api-v0.2.0-rc.1` → `0.2.0-rc.1` (no `latest`, no minor rollup)

## Cutting a release

See `docs/release.md`. Short version:

```sh
# bump crates/api-server/Cargo.toml, commit, merge
git tag api-v0.1.0 -m "api-server v0.1.0"
git push origin api-v0.1.0
# watch https://github.com/adamgell/cmtraceopen-web/actions
```

Then on the deploy host:

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/adamgell/cmtraceopen-api:latest
```

## Implementation notes

- All action versions SHA-pinned (matches ci.yml style).
- `submodules: true` on checkout so the cmtraceopen parser submodule
  is present for the api-server build (same rationale as ci.yml — no
  `recursive` because of unrelated gitlink cruft in the submodule).
- Auth uses the auto-provisioned `GITHUB_TOKEN` with the job's
  `packages: write` permission. No new repo secrets required.
- GHA cache (`type=gha`, `mode=max`) for the buildx layer cache to keep
  repeat runs reasonable.

## Test plan

- [ ] Inspect workflow via `gh workflow view publish-api.yml --repo adamgell/cmtraceopen-web` after merge (verifies it parses server-side).
- [ ] Trigger a `workflow_dispatch` run with `push=false` to validate the multi-arch build end-to-end without uploading an image.
- [ ] Cut a real `api-v0.1.0` tag once the above is green — verify the image shows up under the repo's Packages tab and that `docker pull ghcr.io/adamgell/cmtraceopen-api:0.1.0` works on BigMac.
- [ ] Confirm the GHCR package visibility is set appropriately (Public = no login needed on pull; Private = needs a `read:packages` PAT on BigMac — noted in the runbook).

## Gotchas

- If the first publish fails with a 403 on push, check that
  **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions** allows
  `packages: write` for workflows (or that the job-level permissions
  block here wins — it should, but worth confirming on the first run).
- The GHCR package, once created, may need to be manually flipped to
  Public if that's the desired state — defaults to Private on first
  push.

author: dxnter
body: ## Summary - **Overview admin page redesign** — slim status ribbon, queue alert with exception excerpt + top-pending breakdown via the Laravel 13.6 `Queue::pendingJobs()` API, Login Activity 7×24 heatmap, API Traffic sparkline with p95 latency, consolidated Feature Flags section (with Lockdown moved in), and a Scheduled Tasks table sourced from `schedule:list --json`. Environment / Services / Storage / Error Tracking collapsed into one `Configuration` card. - **Indexed user name search** — new PostgreSQL-only migration adds a stored generated `users.full_name` column plus a `pg_trgm` GIN trigram index. `UserBuilder::searchByName` takes the indexed fast path for comma-less terms; unanchored `ILIKE '%term%'` drops from ~54ms seq scan to ~1ms bitmap-index scan on 50k synthetic rows. Non-PostgreSQL drivers keep the `CONCAT_WS` fallback. `User::fullName` accessor now mirrors the SQL expression so PHP and SQL produce identical values. - **Security fix** — stored XSS in the impersonation global alert. An admin with `CreateUsers` could plant HTML/JS in `first_name`/`last_name`; when a separate admin with `ManageImpersonation` impersonated that user, it executed in the impersonator's session via the shared `{!! $activeAlert['message'] !!}` sink in `northwestern-laravel-ui`. Wrapped with `e()` at the heredoc boundary. - **Bug fix (included with Queue refactor)** — `Overview::getQueueStatus` used to guard pending-job counts behind `queue.default === 'database'`, silently zeroing the alert on Redis-backed projects (the starter default). Now driver-agnostic. CHANGELOG entries folded into the unreleased v2.0.0 section.

## Summary

The WhatsNewModal was doing a raw `fetch('/api/self-upgrade/trigger')` for helm upgrades, bypassing the `useSelfUpgrade` hook. This meant the global `upgradeState` never transitioned from `'idle'` to `'triggering'`, so:

- The **UpdateIndicator** in the navbar never showed the spinning cyan Loader2 icon during background upgrades
- The pulsing cyan dot never appeared
- The user had no visual indication that an upgrade was running after the toast dismissed

**Fix:** Wire the helm path through `useSelfUpgrade().triggerUpgrade()`, which sets the global upgrade state and triggers restart polling. The navbar spinner now appears immediately and transitions through triggering → restarting → complete.

body:
## What changes are proposed in this pull request?

Follow-up to the Apache 2.0 license switch in #198. This PR cleans up license and attribution files across all 5 SDKs.

### 1. Removed stale copyright header from root LICENSE

The root `LICENSE` file had `Copyright 2023 Databricks, Inc. All rights reserved.` prepended to the Apache 2.0 text. This is not standard for Apache 2.0 — the license file should contain only the license text. Copyright attribution belongs in the `NOTICE` file, which all SDKs already have.

### 2. Added LICENSE file to each SDK subdirectory

Since each SDK is independently published to its respective registry, each should have its own `LICENSE` file.

- **npm** auto-includes `LICENSE` from the package directory — without one, the tarball has no license file
- **PyPI/maturin** references `license = {file = "LICENSE"}` in `pyproject.toml` — needs the file to exist locally
- **pkg.go.dev** scans for `LICENSE` in the module directory — without it, marks the module as "no detected license"
- **crates.io** uses the SPDX `license` field which is sufficient, but including the file is standard practice
- **Maven Central** only requires POM metadata, but including the file is standard

This is consistent with how other multi-language SDK monorepos handle it:

- **[delta-rs](https://github.com/delta-io/delta-rs)** (Rust + Python, similar structure) — `LICENSE.txt` in both `python/` and `crates/core/`
- **[AWS SDK for Go v2](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2)** — `LICENSE.txt` in every `service/*/` submodule
- **[Azure SDK for Python](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python)** — `LICENSE` in every `sdk/*/` package directory
- **[Kubernetes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes)** — `LICENSE` in every `staging/src/k8s.io/*/` submodule
- **[tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio)** / **[rustls](https://github.com/rustls/rustls)** — `LICENSE` in every subcrate

### 3. Updated NOTICE files for all SDKs

The NOTICE files were out of date. Changes:

- **Rust**: Added 7 missing runtime deps (`async-trait`, `serde`, `tokio-util`, `hyper-http-proxy`, `hyper-util`, `smallvec`, `bytes`), added optional Arrow Flight section
- **TypeScript**: Added missing deps (`async-trait`, `serde`), reorganized into Rust + JS peer dep sections, added optional Arrow section
- **Go**: Added missing FFI-layer deps, clarified the SDK has no external Go runtime deps, added `arrow-ipc` from FFI layer
- **Java**: Removed phantom transitive deps (gRPC Java, Netty) that aren't direct dependencies, added Apache Arrow (`arrow-vector`), fixed SLF4J license classification (MIT, not CDDL)
- **Python**: Removed incorrectly listed `grpcio` (only `grpcio-tools` is a dev dep — actual gRPC is in Rust via tonic), added optional `pyarrow`, added Rust dependency section (PyO3, tokio, prost, Arrow)

Copyright years in all NOTICE files remain as `2025` — this reflects when the work was first published, not when the license changed. Copyright year records the date of first publication regardless of subsequent license changes.

### 4. Other fixes

- Updated LICENSE links in all SDK READMEs to point to local `LICENSE` instead of the GitHub root URL
- Added `NOTICE` to the TypeScript `package.json` `files` array so it ships in the npm tarball
- Removed `LICENSE` from `python/.gitignore` (was being ignored from when the build process copied it in)

Replaces #61 (closed due to branch protection preventing updates).

## Summary

This PR adds forward-compatibility for PHP 8.4 and PHP 8.5 while keeping PHP 8.2/8.3 support.

The last PHP 8.4 pass (#34) landed in 1.9.0, but a handful of spots still rely on silent null/false coercion that becomes a hard error on PHP 8.5 (where several long-standing deprecations are being promoted to TypeErrors, e.g. passing null to internal string functions, or passing a non-parseable string to `DateTime::modify()`).

cc @rhoerr @dadolun95 @SamueleMartini — happy to iterate if you want to tag this as **2.1.2** after merge.

## Fixes

- **`Plugin/Adminhtml{Category,Cms,Product}BeforeSavePlugin`**: cast the return value of `preg_replace()` to string before `strtolower()`. `preg_replace` can return `null` on failure, and `strtolower(null)` is a `TypeError` on PHP 8.5.
- **`Helper/Service::encodePageBuilderHtmlBox`**: cast `DOMDocument::saveHTML()` results to string before feeding them to `html_entity_decode()` / string concatenation. `saveHTML()` can return `false`; PHP 8.5 enforces the `string` parameter of `html_entity_decode` strictly.
- **`Helper/ModuleConfig::getTranslationExpirationDate`**: cast the retranslation-period scope value to int before building the `DateTime::modify()` expression. Previously an unset/empty config produced `- days`, which becomes a `DateMalformedStringException` on PHP 8.5.
- **`Setup/Patch/Data/MigrateConfigPaths`**: cast the legacy scope value to string before re-encrypting, since `EncryptorInterface::encrypt()` now requires a strict string on PHP 8.5.
- **Nullable values used as array index**: cast to `string`/`int` before using as array key to avoid PHP 8.5 null array key deprecation (follow-up to #61 feedback on mage-os-lab/module-widgetkit#13).
- **`composer.json`**: widen the PHP constraint to `>=8.2 <8.6` so Composer resolves cleanly on PHP 8.4 and 8.5.

No behavior change on PHP 8.2/8.3 — all casts are no-ops on valid input.

## Suggested tag

`2.1.2` (patch — backwards compatible bug fixes only).

- [x] Manual: translate a category / product / CMS page with a populated `url_key` / `identifier` on PHP 8.5
- [x] Manual: run the translation cron on PHP 8.5 with a valid retranslation period set

## Description
ops.zeros, ops.ones, ops.empty, and ops.full previously built the output shape by calling ov_opset.constant(shape, Type.i32) directly. This crashes when any element of the shape is an OpenVINOKerasTensor scalar, returned by ops.shape(x) on a tensor with dynamic dimensions, such as one produced during graph construction with a dynamic batch axis.

Fix: All four ops now call shape_to_ov_output() (introduced in #22692), which handles mixed static/dynamic shape tuples by building per-dim constants and concatenating them into a single i32 shape tensor. A guard is also added to shape_to_ov_output to raise a clear error if None appears in the shape tuple, directing callers to use ops.shape(x) rather than x.shape to obtain a runtime-resolved shape.

Note: This PR does not revert #22681. The _parameterize_data dynamic batch workaround in the trainer is left in place; fixing that properly will be tracked separately.

## Summary

Second pre-launch hardening pass. Builds on PR #1's security fixes with role enforcement, structural cleanup, and extended audit coverage.

### Scope (reviewer-approved)

| ID | Fix | Status |
|----|-----|--------|
| **H1** | Full role matrix (OWNER/ADMIN/MEMBER) enforcement | ✅ |
| **H5** | Dockerfile runs as non-root UID 1000 | ✅ |
| **H6** | `datetime.utcnow()` → `now_utc()` helper | ✅ |
| **H4** | Audit count query uses `func.count()` | ✅ |
| **M4** | `/health` checks DB connectivity (503 on failure) | ✅ |
| **Q2** | 25+ copies of team-ownership check → one `verified_team` dep | ✅ |
| **Q1** | `create_issue` / `_create_issue_inner` merged (-80 lines) | ✅ |
| **S4** | Audit coverage for rule/label/project/team mutations | ✅ (partial — user/membership deferred) |
| **H2** | Structured logging across the app | ⏳ PR 2.5 |
| **Q4+S5** | Uniform error envelope via exception handler | ⏳ PR 2.5 |

### Role matrix (H1)

| Action                            | OWNER | ADMIN | MEMBER |
|-----------------------------------|-------|-------|--------|
| CRUD issues, comments             |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ✅    |
| Create/update labels, projects    |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ✅    |
| Delete labels, projects           |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ❌    |
| Create/update/delete rules        |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ❌    |
| Create workflow states            |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ❌    |
| Add members                       |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ❌    |
| Update team settings              |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ❌    |
| `POST /teams`                     |  ✅   |  ❌   |  ❌    |
| View audit trail (all users)      |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ❌    |
| View audit trail (self only)      |  ✅   |  ✅   |  ✅    |

Enforced via `require_role_in_authed_team()` / `require_role_in_path_team()` dep factories in `api/deps.py`. MEMBER audit-trail access is transparently filtered to `user_id = self`.

### Client-visible contract changes

Role-gated endpoints now return **403 "Insufficient role"** when the caller lacks the required role:

- `DELETE /labels/{id}`, `DELETE /projects/{id}` — ADMIN+
- `POST /teams/{id}/rules`, `PATCH /rules/{id}`, `DELETE /rules/{id}` — ADMIN+
- `POST /teams/{id}/users` (add members) — ADMIN+
- `POST /teams/{id}/states` — ADMIN+
- `PATCH /teams/{id}` (settings) — ADMIN+

Additionally:
- `POST /api/v1/teams` auto-adds the caller as OWNER of the new team (previously the new team had zero members — unusable).
- Missing `X-API-Key` now returns 401 consistently (was 422).
- `/api/v1/health` now returns **503** if the DB is unreachable (previously returned 200 regardless).
- Every CUD on rules, labels, projects, and team settings writes an audit entry; the entry is visible via `GET /audit?entity_type=rule` etc.

### Bonus bits

- **Auto-OWNER on team creation.** The caller of `POST /teams` is now added as OWNER of the new team in the same transaction, so follow-up `POST /users` calls can succeed.
- **Dep consolidation.** `verified_team(team_id)` replaces 25+ manual `if authed_team.id != team_id: raise 403` checks. Security-critical boilerplate now lives in exactly one place — missing a copy in a new endpoint is no longer possible.
- **`now_utc()` helper** (`src/taskstore/utils/time.py`) replaces `datetime.utcnow()` project-wide. Silences the Python 3.12 deprecation warning. DB columns remain tz-naive for now; migrating to `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE` is a planned follow-up.

### Tests

- **Before:** 106 passing (PR 1's state after EM cleanup)
- **After:** 126 passing (+20 regression tests)
- **Warnings:** 1082 → 0

New test files:
- `tests/test_roles.py` — 15 tests covering the full role matrix (member-cannot-X, admin-can-Y, owner-only-Z, plus member-can-do-normal-things positive paths).
- `tests/test_audit_coverage.py` — 5 tests asserting audit entries exist for rule/label/project/team mutations.

Modified test files migrate fixtures to use the `/setup`-created OWNER user, since many endpoints now require `X-User-Id` for auth.

### Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/` — 126 passed, 0 warnings
- [x] MEMBER cannot delete labels, projects, rules
- [x] MEMBER cannot add members, create states, update team settings
- [x] MEMBER audit response contains only their own entries
- [x] ADMIN can do all ADMIN+ gated actions
- [x] OWNER can do everything
- [x] Post-creation, new team owner can add users + act as OWNER
- [x] `/health` returns 503 when DB is down (manual)
- [x] Dockerfile runs uvicorn as UID 1000

### Out of scope (PR 2.5)

- **H2** — structured logging across the app. (Minimal `logging.getLogger` usage is in `rules/evaluator.py` already; broadening to auth events, 5xx paths, etc. is next.)
- **Q4 + S5** — uniform error envelope via FastAPI exception handler + stripping internal enum values from error details.
- **S4 completion** — audit coverage on `POST /users` / membership changes. (The endpoint exists but has no audit yet; role changes don't have an endpoint yet either.)

### Reviewer context

Implements the second-tier items approved on the original punch-list. The role matrix is the shape reviewer confirmed + the MEMBER audit self-filter addition. Broad test rewrites were needed because many fixtures relied on unauthenticated `POST /users` and unauthenticated `POST /teams` — both now correctly require auth.
